commits.message:
[agents] Reuse holistic review sessions and set capacity to eight (#10134)

Set the correctness and holistic review profiles to eight concurrent
sessions each. Both profiles retain the merged Claude Opus 5.5
configuration.

Route initial and follow-up holistic reviews through a stable per-PR
Loom channel. A later delivery updates the existing live session instead
of launching a parallel reviewer; the reused session fetches and checks
out the requested immutable head before reviewing. The existing run keys
still limit automatic holistic review to an initial run and one
follow-up. Correctness and holistic review remain separate profiles.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[agents] Bound automatic review sessions per pull request (#10133)

Use durable per-PR keys to allow one correctness review, one initial
holistic review, one holistic follow-up, and one deslop run. The
follow-up runs on synchronize only when the head commit changes more
than 100 lines against its parent and the PR meets the existing holistic
review eligibility gate. Repeated events return the existing run;
further reviews and retries require an explicit session launch.

Use `claude-opus-5-5` for the correctness and holistic review profiles
when the Loom deployment policy is applied.

commits.message:
[marina] Improve app discovery, navigation, and data guidance (#10132)

Replace Marina's growing row of app links with a title bar and
searchable app drawer. Keep each app's navigation on a separate row,
with keyboard focus management, Escape dismissal, and a layout that
accommodates long app names and narrow screens. The directory presents
alphabetized cards with names and descriptions, and the checked-in
manifests describe what each app does in two sentences.

The shared AppBar also works without Marina’s Shell component or a
directory fetch. Filer adopts it with a link back to Marina; isolated
and public applets do not gain access to the private directory API. The
agent panel uses the remaining viewport height instead of assuming a
fixed header height. Uploaded applets retain their published metadata
and UI until republished; this change does not deploy or republish them.

TaskTrove filters now reuse cached metadata row groups instead of
reopening object storage for those groups. Cold groups still read only
the columns needed by the filter. The cache remains bounded and
process-local, and task archives remain in object storage.

The caching audit covered the five checked-in apps and the 12 active
uploaded applets on October 14, 2026. For uploaded apps without
checked-in backend sources, the evidence is their published frontend and
read-only enumeration of their own Postgres tables; table presence does
not establish refresh frequency, and an empty schema does not rule out a
cache elsewhere.

search index outside serving startup. |

through a separate ingestion job. Sample and artifact TTL caches remain
process-local; copying payloads into Postgres needs size and reuse
measurements. |

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[haliax] Run the tile-map ragged_dot kernels on NVIDIA GPUs (#10098)

Hopper (sm_90) and data-center Blackwell (sm_100 and sm_103) GPUs now
run the Pallas-Triton grouped GEMM behind `ragged_dot` with the tile-map
kernels from #10009, which AMD Instinct GPUs already use. Until now they
ran the group-grid kernels, which launch a full row grid for every
expert. Other NVIDIA GPUs, such as A100 and consumer Blackwell (sm_120),
keep the group-grid kernels: the tuned configs need about 192 KiB of
shared memory per block in bf16, more than those GPUs allow. Block
configs were swept on H100 and GB200 at the June (G=32, K and N of
1280-2560) and Mixtral-like (G=8, 4096x14336) expert shapes. On H100,
drhs (the weight gradient) uses 128x128x32 blocks below 2048 rows per
expert; with the 128x256x64 blocks it uses above that, it was 4-8%
slower than group-grid at 512 rows per expert.

Per call in bf16, against group-grid, at M from 16384 to 196608 rows
with balanced and Zipf-skewed routing:

| GPU | Tile-map faster | Speedup |
|---|---|---|
| GB200 | 54 of 54 cases | 1.03-2.47x |
| H100 | 49 of 54 cases | 1.04-2.50x |

The other 5 H100 cases are drhs at 512 and 1024 rows per expert, at
0.98-1.00x.

On one 8xH100 node, an 8-layer June model (batch 64, 8-way expert
parallelism, full recompute) took 0.817 s per step with tile-map and
0.848-0.849 s in three group-grid runs, a 3.9% throughput gain, with the
same loss after 20 steps.

`lib/levanter/scripts/bench/bench_ragged_dot_triton.py --kernel-families
group_grid tile_map` reproduces the balanced per-call timings.

Add aligned Snowball checkpoint merging and calibration (#9974)

Add aligned Snowball/Grug checkpoint merging and coefficient/curvature
calibration. Parent tensor names, shapes, dtypes, and expert identities
must already align; the tools do not infer expert permutations.

Constrained exports preserve the original input checkpoint's (Base)
metadata, tensor layout, and at least 75% of its scalar weights
bit-for-bit. A temporary incomplete marker blocks Marin checkpoint reads
until the actual change cap passes and the audit is saved outside the
checkpoint and read back. Successful finalization removes the marker,
preserving Base's original file inventory. Every serial stage is checked
against original Base. The historical unconstrained exporter remains
available separately.

Calibration uses one pinned runtime launcher with an explicit module
selection and optional hash-verified SkyRL patch. Chunk allocation
preserves each trainer's scoring and tie ordering.

The [Campaign 2 artifact
archive](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Model-Merging-Artifacts-2026.10.09/tree/1ef199578aeec9f08e142a8dd760d44658264be4/campaign2-recipes)
contains 54 recipes and [unrounded result
evidence](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Model-Merging-Artifacts-2026.10.09/blob/1ef199578aeec9f08e142a8dd760d44658264be4/campaign2-recipes/results-evidence.json)
for 48 completed candidates. The [evaluation
release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Model-Merging-Artifacts-2026.10.09/blob/c4fb17eb44005e01cbb3d5b38c672a2ffa473880/artifacts/inputs/RELEASE.md)
records the BFCL/NUPA evaluation commands. DARE-TIES-02 scored 45.53
BFCL and 0.00 NUPA200 while changing 6.04% of Base parameters.
Non-target retention was not evaluated. Broader benchmark comparisons
are recorded in #9975. Historical calibration tensors and raw evaluation
transcripts remain private, so refitting/rerunning is supported but
exact calibrated-output replay is not guaranteed.

Part of #9975.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[grug] Run the ring EP MoE test's collectives synchronously on AMD GPUs (#10107)

On AMD GPUs, the forward and gradient jits in
`test_moe_mlp_ep_backends_match_dense_value_and_gradients_when_available`
now pass the compiler option
`xla_gpu_disable_async_collectives=ALLCOLLECTIVES`, so each device runs
one collective at a time. The test checks for the ROCm backend, so this
covers both MI300X and MI350X. CUDA and TPU keep XLA's default
collective schedule, as in training. Only the test changes.

On 8x MI300X without the fix, the ring-backend cases `[all_valid-ring]`
and `[padded-ring]` hung until the pytest timeout in 10 of 52 runs,
where each run is one fresh pytest process for one case. The hangs
happened on both cluster nodes, and on main from both before and after
#9860 added `ring_gather_combine`. The ring forward launches its
psum-scatter over the expert axis (a 2-device RCCL communicator)
asynchronously on a second stream. The drop-count psum over all 8
devices does not depend on it, so it runs on the compute stream while
the psum-scatter is in flight. In the backward, the weight-gradient psum
over the data axis (4 devices) overlaps the same psum-scatter. Because
the two collectives run on different streams, nothing fixes which one
each GPU runs first, so the order can differ between ranks and between
runs. In hung runs, rocgdb showed one RCCL kernel running on every GPU
and work pending on a second hardware queue, consistent with each rank
waiting for peers that are in the other collective. NCCL documents that
operations on different communicators can deadlock when ranks issue them
in different orders ([Using multiple NCCL communicators
concurrently](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/usage/communicators.html#using-multiple-nccl-communicators-concurrently)).

On MI300X with the fix, the two cases passed 24 of 24 runs (12 per
case), and RCCL logs showed each device launching all of its collectives
on one stream. The same flag set through `XLA_FLAGS` on unmodified main
also passed 24 of 24.

On 8x MI350X, unmodified main hung in 2 of 24 runs (12 per case), back
to back on one node, after every GPU had launched the same overlapping
collectives. In both hangs only one GPU still had an RCCL kernel running
and queued work, while the other seven had drained their queues. On
MI300X every GPU was still waiting, so the MI350X hang may have a
different cause that synchronous collectives do not prevent. With the
fix, MI350X passed 8 of 8 runs. At main's hang rate, 8 runs in a row
pass about half the time without the fix, so this does not yet show that
the fix holds on MI350X.

On 8x H100, unmodified main passed all 48 runs (24 per case), although
NCCL logs showed the same overlap. NCCL's warning applies to NVIDIA GPUs
too, so CUDA may still hang at a lower rate; 48 clean runs put that rate
below about 6% per run at 95% confidence. CUDA keeps XLA's default
schedule so the test compiles as training does there.

Training still runs the ring EP backends with async collectives, so AMD
training could hit the same overlap. We have not seen this hang in
training or measured what synchronous collectives would cost there. Only
one ragged all-to-all EP configuration in
`experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/train.py` forces synchronous collectives,
after overlapping collectives there hung or gave run-to-run different
gradients on GB200.

Part of #9812

---------

Co-authored-by: Amy Sartran <users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[agents] Add a holistic Loom review lane and agent-PR deslop (#10127)

Add a whole-change review lane for pull requests. The
`pr-holistic-review`
Loom profile runs the `claude` agent with the `fable` model and the new
`review-pr-holistic` skill, which asks eight questions a hunk-scoped
review
cannot: fit with existing repository concepts, a smaller abstraction,
consequences in unchanged code (silent critical defaults, failures
encoded as
values), tests hidden behind skipped markers, claims versus evidence,
related
pull requests, test value under TESTING.md, and scope. The session posts
one
numbered packet ending in a `marin-holistic-review` marker and logs
findings
through `log_stats.py` under tool `review-pr-holistic`.

`ops-loom-holistic-review.yaml` launches the session from the trusted
default
branch for a non-draft same-repository PR whose author has write access,
when
the change has at least 250 changed lines or adds a class, dataclass, or
`Protocol` under `lib/*/src/` or `experiments/`. Unlike
`ops-loom-review.yaml`
it also fires on `synchronize`, with per-PR cancellation; the session
skips a
delta under 100 changed lines, a delta of fixtures or documentation
only, and a
delta made only of `Deslop` commits.

A `deslop` job in `ops-loom-github.yaml` launches a `github-automation`
session when a holistic packet lands on a PR carrying `agent-generated`,
or
when a maintainer review contains `deslop`. That session applies only
the
packet's mechanical items and the `noslop` skill, pushes one `Deslop`
commit
after the narrow checks pass, and posts suggestions without pushing on
PRs
without the label.

On PR #10077 the opening-head correctness and lint passes found five
bugs and
eight catalog findings; two later interactive Fable reviews found 22
structural items and 10 tests to drop, all resolved in one push each.
Running
the skill blind with Opus reviewers over that head and seven other
recent
large PRs reproduced 13 of the 16 applicable #10077 items and matched 28
of
45 human structural comments overall, with the misses concentrated in
hunk-local nits the lint catalog already owns. Trial packets, scoring,
and
the design record are in the Loom artifact `holistic-pr-review` on the
`weaver/better-pr-code-review` branch.

The Loom stack must be applied before the GitHub stack so
`LOOM_PR_HOLISTIC_REVIEW_PROFILE` exists when the workflow first runs.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[grug] Add a Pallas-Triton flash attention for AMD GPUs (#10014)

Add `gpu_pallas_triton_flash`, an opt-in fused causal attention for Grug
on AMD GPUs, where Grug has no fused kernel. Existing backends are
unchanged.

These kernels use Pallas-Triton, which JAX 0.11 deprecates; Mosaic GPU,
the replacement JAX suggests for Pallas, does not support ROCm. #9853
ports the same kernels to Triton launched through
`jax_triton.triton_call`, 12-24% faster per layer on MI300X and MI350X,
but jax-triton kernels hang multi-GPU training on ROCm today. On a
kernel's first launch, jaxlib 0.11.1 reads the compiled hsaco from a
temporary file and deletes it without holding its cache lock, so when
the 8 GPUs of one process launch together, all but one fail and the step
stalls at the next collective (evidence and a standalone repro in
#9853). This PR lands the Pallas-Triton version so AMD runs can use
fused attention now. #9853 replaces it once AMD's jax fork, which builds
the ROCm plugin, fixes the race.

The kernel reduces each mask to one inclusive key lower bound per query,
`max(segment start, q - W + 1)` for window `W`. Key blocks outside
`[lower bound, q]` are skipped, and blocks fully inside it skip the mask
computation. GQA indexes the shared KV head instead of repeating K/V.
Under a mesh, batch and heads may be sharded; sequence and head_dim may
not. The lower bounds are computed here and not with the FA4/CuTe
helpers, which treat negative segment IDs as padding and would make the
ROCm path import the CuTe backend.

One layer's forward plus backward at the June per-GPU shape (8 x 4096
tokens, 20 query heads, 5 KV heads, head_dim 128, bf16), median of three
interleaved rounds in one process, jax 0.11.1 (jobs 457836, 457837):

| Mask | GPU | reference | `gpu_pallas_triton_flash` |
|---|---|---|---|
| window 2048 | MI350X | 20.19 ms | 6.77 ms |
| causal | MI350X | 22.26 ms | 10.04 ms |
| window 2048 | MI300X | 31.17 ms | 12.04 ms |
| causal | MI300X | 32.32 ms | 17.28 ms |

The full June model at batch 64 on 8x MI350X goes from 2.426 s to 1.853
s per step (9.32% to 12.20% MFU) with jaxlib 0.11.0, peak memory falls
from 184 to 158 GiB, and the loss matches the reference run
(https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9812#issuecomment-6027803714).

Value and gradient parity tests against `reference_attention` pass on
MI350X (job 458164) and in the Pallas interpreter on CPU (job 458155),
which is the only way CI runs them. On MI300X the bf16 cases pass and
the f32 cases skip (job 458163): Triton runs the kernels'
default-precision f32 dots in TF32 on gfx942 and NVIDIA GPUs, about
2.7e-3 off the f32 reference.

Each run of equal segment IDs is one document, so a segment ID that
reappears after a different ID starts a new document;
`reference_attention` lets the two runs attend to each other. Masks that
carry FA4 precomputed bounds are rejected, which excludes the
moe_hero_ep, moe_hero_fsdp and fast_track variants.

Part of #9812

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[task-curation] Declare grader requirements, files and env (#10104)

An `Environment` declares what a grader environment wants, and the build
resolves it:

- `requirements`: exact `name==version` pins or `name @ https://...`
URLs naming a commit. The build compiles them with `uv pip compile
--generate-hashes --exclude-newer <date>` and stores the lock in the
artifact; the cutoff date is a constant in the build module and part of
the identity, so every build of an identity resolves the same transitive
packages. `grader.in` and `grader.lock` are deleted; the pins live in
`datasets/environments.py` as per-scorer tuples, and the four previously
unpinned entries take the versions the lock had resolved.
- `files`: absolute guest paths, each receiving a member of an https
archive pinned by URL and SHA-256. The build downloads, verifies and
extracts the member into the build context. A built image gets `COPY
files/ /`; the artifact stores `files.tar` and `environment.json`
(paths, archive digest, env) for the worker. A path under a host system
directory, which bubblewrap binds read-only, or inside another placed
path is rejected at declaration.
- `env`: variables for the grader in both placements, rendered as `ENV`
lines in the image and set on the worker sandbox.
- `apt`, `image` and `dockerfile` are unchanged.

The NLTK-only `data` slot is gone. `GRADER_PACKAGES` places the English
`punkt_tab` tokenizer from a pinned `nltk_data` archive at
`/srv/nltk_data/tokenizers/punkt_tab/english` with
`NLTK_DATA=/srv/nltk_data`. `wordnet` had no consumer and is dropped.
The Punkt models carry no license in `nltk_data`, so the tables are
fetched at build time rather than checked in.

The worker runtime downloads the lock and hashes it itself instead of
reading a digest from the artifact record, and reads `environment.json`
and `files.tar` beside the lock when present; the lock and archive
digests both enter the cached environment's identity.
`taskcompendium.runtime.local` loses `LockEnvironment`, the
`.artifact.json` reader and the NLTK downloader. The artifact record
keeps only the identity and the built image digest.

shellbox's `HostImage` gains `mounts`, host files or directories shown
read-only at another guest path with a plain `--ro-bind`. The local
backend treats its read-only directories as mounts at their own paths
and refuses a guest path inside a system directory, inside another
mount, or as the workdir; uploads to a mounted path are rejected. QUICK
mode records the lock URL the environment's artifact would have under
the active artifact prefix.

Placement does not change: the base grader and compiler environments run
in bubblewrap on the Zephyr worker, and Lean runs in its built image.
The first `python -m experiments.post_training.task_curation.images
--all` build verifies the `punkt_tab` archive digest against the live
download.

The calibration, load and replay reports that #10077 checked in under
`scripts/fixtures` are removed; nothing in code or tests reads them, and
the PR that cites a report links it from an artifact prefix instead. The
labelled cases, normalized task snapshots and provenance the calibration
script consumes stay.

commits.author: muchanem
commits.message:
[shellbox] Stop retrying an Iris exec after the machine closes (#9844)

`IrisMachine` retries an exec that the controller refused for a full
exec pool (#9828), under Iris's 30-minute RPC retry budget (#9780). When
a command's timeout expires during that loop, `run()` closes the machine
and reports `TIMED_OUT`, but `asyncio.wait_for` cannot stop the worker
thread, so it could keep resending the command and have it admitted
after the caller returned. Each attempt now checks whether the machine
has closed and raises instead of sending. `close()` sets that flag
before it terminates the job, so no attempt starts after a timed-out
`run` returns.

Reported by the Codex review on #9780 after it merged.

[grug] Switch the hero to 16K context with qk_mult 1.48 (#10101)

Switch the hero from 4K to 16K context with `qk_mult` 1.48 on all
layers. The new run `hero-ctx16k-step257k` forks `hero-mfu30-step231k`
at its permanent `step-257553`, where the parent stopped on 2026-10-13.
Tokens per rack per update, the 390251-step schedule, and the optimizer
stay the same, so the batch drops from 11264 to 2816 sequences on 11
racks.

`HERO_MODEL` gets `max_seq_len=16384` and `qk_mult=1.48`.
`HERO_CONTEXT_PHASES` records the 4K phase ending at step 257553, and
`HERO_FLOPS_BASELINE_TOTAL` is 1.7792877262736668e24, the parent's
`throughput/total_gflops` × 1e9 at W&B `_step` 257552 (`global_step`
257552). `trigger_hero.sh` hands off from
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-mfu30-step231k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-257553`
(permanent, `metadata.json` step 257553) and forks W&B at
`hero-mfu30-step231k?_step=257552`; `current_run.py` names the child.

`build_ladder_run` now uses the checked-in history for d6144 by itself
instead of relying on `main()`, and it refuses an explicit `num_steps`
while a history is in effect, because the prior phases' data stages are
rebuilt from the schedule length. The diagnostics launcher and restore
benchmark take their default batch from the hero's tokens per rack at
the model's context length (256 sequences per rack at 16K); the old
fixed 1024-sequence default would have put four times the hero's load on
a rack. `HERO_EP_BATCH_SIZE` is replaced by `HERO_TOKENS_PER_RACK` and
`hero_rack_batch_size` in `hero_recipe.py`.

In 100-step arms at 16K from permanent `step-252000` on the 11 hero
racks (#9615), the dropless eval loss after step 252100 was 1.81349 at

the global layers only. The differences are within eval noise, so we
keep the YaRN-style value 1.3 × (0.1·ln 4 + 1). Those arms also ran the
16K dropless eval on 11 racks at 123.4 GiB peak memory, about 30.6% MFU,
and a drop fraction falling to about 1.2e-3.

A dry build of the exact `trigger_hero.sh` launch gives 16K, `qk_mult`

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[task-curation] Add Dockerfile toolchain fragments and a Lean grader image (#10088)

An `Environment` can name a checked-in, self-contained Dockerfile
fragment that installs a toolchain the package lock cannot provide. A
fragment forces placement in a built image, its bytes enter the
environment identity, the build refuses an untracked fragment, and the
generated Dockerfile runs its lines after the apt step and before the
lock sync so toolchain layers stay cached across lock changes. A
fragment may use only `ARG`, `ENV` and `RUN`; the declaration refuses
`FROM`, `USER`, `WORKDIR`, `SHELL`, `COPY`, `ADD`, `ENTRYPOINT` and
`CMD`, which would replace the base, break the generated package steps
or change the grader container. The existing build CLI pushes the image
to the public iris-task package and records its digest, so pinning
follows from the identity.

The environment artifact record now carries the identity, the built
image digest, and the lock digest and `data` the worker runtime reads
back from the record beside the lock. The copies of `apt`, the Python
version, the base image, the fragment digest and the pushed tag are
gone; the identity already hashes them and nothing read them.

`LEAN_GRADER_PACKAGES` uses the fragment to add elan, Lean
leanprover/lean4 v4.12.0 and Mathlib v4.12.0 (commit 809c3fb3) with
prebuilt oleans at `/lean4/my_project`, the layout the NeMo Skills
sandbox uses, so the vendored Lean feedback parser finds diagnostics at
the path it expects. `LocalLeanSandbox` compiles a proof with `lake env
lean` in that project and answers with the NeMo Skills server's `lean4`
response fields. The Nemotron Ultra Lean grader can then run inside the
network-denied grader sandbox instead of calling an in-cluster sandbox
service. This PR adds the image and the sandbox class only; the Lean
converter and controls land in #10077.

The image built locally in 109 s for the Lean and Mathlib layer (2.39
GB; 3.8 GB total). With networking disabled and as uid 65534, a Mathlib
`simp` proof completes in 4 s warm and 38 s cold, a bad tactic fails
with the diagnostic at the project path, and a `sorry` proof completes
with the warning the status parser maps to `has_sorry`. The cold time
exceeds the vendored scorer's default 30 s timeout, so the converter
needs a larger timeout. The Lean and Mathlib pins match every NeMo
Skills sandbox build since October 2024; the private sandbox image
MarinSkyRL pins by digest does not record its revision, so the pin is
not confirmed against that exact image. No artifact for the environment
has been built or pushed yet.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[rl] Integrate sampled grading with curation and Atlas (#10075)

FULL RL curation now samples the resulting TaskSpec parquet and stage
evidence, prepares bounded packets with Zephyr, and obtains one
structured GLM judgment per item. The default sample contains up to 100
retained tasks and 20 excluded diagnostics. SAMPLE campaigns opt in with
`--assess`. The artifact graph connects curation, packet preparation and
grading; a rubric or model change reuses curation outputs.

Executable controls and downstream grades have separate policies. A
control sample passing at least 95% allows curation to skip unsampled
controls. Otherwise it validates eligible tasks individually, retaining
passes, rejecting failures and deferring unavailable controls.
Checkpoints preserve completed trials on retries. Downstream grading
labels a source Good when at least 80% of judgments are Good and Bad
when more than 20% are Bad. If neither threshold is met, fewer than 80%
conclusive judgments means Unknown; otherwise the label is Some issues.
Completed curation that retains no tasks is Bad. Excluded diagnostics do
not affect the source grade, and grading does not change task admission.
Large tasks retain bounded summaries with explicit omissions.

The typed catalog owns source declarations, assessment keys,
populations, judgments and archived evidence. Atlas reads Postgres
through an explicit staged catalog load. SQL computes counts and grades;
the browser handles filtering, sorting and CSV export. Unchanged
snapshots skip loading. Inventory-only sources carry a skip reason. The
separate reassessment path, manual verifier declarations and legacy
review-publication code path are removed; historical manual reviews
remain archived.

The completed campaign covers all 146 curation pipelines in an inventory
of 206 sources. The selected catalog snapshot is
`8c5d247ef6c2416fb3d14b2f159f74c4`: 63 Good, 40 Some issues, 43 Bad and
0 Unknown. Forty-one Bad sources retained no tasks; two exceeded the Bad
judgment threshold. All retained samples have TaskSpecs and conclusive
judgments.

| Sample cohort | Items | Good | Some issues | Bad | Unknown |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Retained | 10,430 | 8,513 | 1,458 | 459 | 0 |
| Excluded diagnostics | 1,677 | 235 | 150 | 977 | 315 |

The local AIME24/SVAMP rollout took 6.4 seconds for six SAMPLE judgments
(five retained tasks and one excluded diagnostic) and 0.33 seconds on an
unchanged repeat. The first aggregation left 72 sources Unknown; 41
became Bad under the zero-output rule and 31 were regraded after packet
and control-validation fixes. A final campaign reused those 31
assessment graphs and published one catalog snapshot with the other 115
assessments retained. The regional archive audit checked all 12,107
packets in 125 seconds: 284.7 MB total and 50.8 KB at p95. Bulk GCS
processing stayed in us-central2. [Campaign
outputs](https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/marin-us-central2/rl-data-curation-assessment/2026-10-12-campaign/campaigns)
include `updated-grade-report.md` with every source's sample scores,
control outcomes and inference measurements. Permanent catalog and
evidence outputs are under
`gs://marin-us-central2/rl-data-curation-assessment/2026-10-12-campaign/campaigns/`.

The live Atlas applet remains on its previous revision because Marina
requires its current publisher to deploy the bundle and load this
catalog.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[levanter] Bound in-flight W&B metric host copies (#10024)

Keep at most 8 device-to-host copies ahead of the value being read when
converting a W&B payload. #9600 started a copy for every array leaf at
once.

PJRT's GPU client finishes pending copies on a work queue
(`pjrt_async_work_runner`) that starts a thread whenever queued work
exceeds its idle threads and never stops one. A step's outputs become
ready together, so prefetching a watch-step payload released thousands
of copies at once and grew the queue by hundreds of threads in every
process. The threads inherit the name `py_xla_callback` because their
own name exceeds Linux's 15-character limit. On a one-rack restore of
the hero run, each training process grew from 1 to about 1,700
`py_xla_callback` threads within 20 minutes, about 3,400 threads in
total. Each blocking py-spy dump pauses every thread, so dumps took
about 3.5x longer; #9998 makes Iris's periodic dumps non-blocking.

A single-node GB200 repro (4 processes, d768 MoE, watch every 10 steps)
puts the growth at #9600: its parent and main with #9600 reverted keep 1
`py_xla_callback` thread per process, and #9600 has 318–424. With 2,000
scalars converted by `_convert_metrics_to_wandb_loggable` on one GPU:

| | `py_xla_callback` threads | conversion time |
|---|---|---|
| before #9600 | 1 | 60 ms |
| #9600 | 418 | 31 ms |
| this change | 2 | 33 ms |
